me: LEGO uses a relation-centric, affine-transformation-based hardware representation that maps temporal/spatial iteration indices to computation indices via linear matrices, fully decoupling computation logic, data paths, and memory from one another. The LEGO frontend solves integer linear equations to find FU interconnections exploiting data reuse, runs a Minimum Spanning Tree (Chu-Liu/Edmonds algorithm) to prune redundant connections, and applies a BFS-based heuristic to plan direct interconnections across multiple fused dataflows with conflict-free banked memory. t: Efficient Optimization with Encoded Ising Models

me: The Encoded Ising Model (E-I model) extends the standard Ising model by inserting a digital encoding circuit between the solver and the energy landscape, restricting the search space to only feasible states without penalty terms. The Fuse software framework provides a high-level API to describe such constrained functions and automatically lowers them to a p-computer target. The encoding circuit uses a combinational logic layer that maps solver spin states to legal variable assignments, reducing the fraction of iterations spent on infeasible solutions by orders of magnitude.

me: ZAC (Zoned Architecture Compiler) introduces qubit reuse as a core optimization: qubits already in the entanglement zone are kept there if an immediate entangling gate is pending, avoiding round-trip movement to storage. ZAC additionally introduces novel data placement strategies that anticipate future gate scheduling needs, a new instruction scheduling algorithm for zoned operations, a flexible specification language for diverse zoned architectures, and ZAIR, an intermediate representation capturing zoned-architecture-specific constraints. The compiler is evaluated on circuits showing 22x fidelity improvement over monolithic architectures.

t: EDA: Energy-Efficient Inter-Layer Model Compilation for Edge DNN Inference Acceleration

An inter-layer cost model rapidly determines the optimal operator traversal depth for each subgraph given the available on-chip SRAM. EDA then manages the on-chip shared memory space to prevent overflow, and applies operator grouping to improve MAC unit and SRAM space utilization. The resulting compilation avoids both excessive DRAM traffic (from too-deep traversal) and under-utilization (from too-shallow traversal).

t: Exploring the Performance Improvement of Tensor Processing Engines through Transformation in the Bit-weight Dimension of MACs

There is no systematic framework for reasoning about and transforming the bit-level structure of MACs to improve TPE PPA.
me: The paper introduces a novel bit-weight dimension perspective on matrix multiplication and a finer-grained TPE notation based on matrix triple loops that exposes the internal MAC structure. Four optimization techniques are derived from transformations in this bit-weight space: they target timing, area, and power at the PE microarchitecture level. The design is implemented in RTL using SMIC-28nm and applied to four canonical TPE architectures (systolic array, 3D-Cube, multiplier-adder tree, 2D-Matrix) and a bit-slice architecture.
nv: A new algebraic notation capturing the bit-weight dimension of MACs enables four distinct PE microarchitecture optimizations that are orthogonal to existing dataflow or operand-reuse strategies.

t: Choco-Q: Commute Hamiltonian-based QAOA for Constrained Binary Optimization
pb: Existing QAOA approaches for constrained binary optimization based on penalty terms or cyclic Hamiltonian simulation fail to encode arbitrary linear constraints, yielding near-zero success rates (as low as 0.02%) and long end-to-end latency. Decomposing the resulting Hamiltonians into deployable quantum circuits has exponential time and memory complexity.
me: Choco-Q encodes constraints by selecting a driver Hamiltonian that commutes with the constraint operator (the commute Hamiltonian), exploiting the Heisenberg picture to guarantee that constraint expectation values remain invariant during quantum evolution, achieving 100% in-constraints rate. Three optimization passes reduce circuit complexity for NISQ deployment: (1) Hamiltonian serialization decomposes the global commute Hamiltonian into independent local sub-Hamiltonians (proven via Lemma 1 to preserve constraint satisfaction), reducing circuit depth from ~4000 to ~24; (2) equivalent decomposition converts each local commute Hamiltonian into control-phase gates and CX gates with linear O(n) time complexity and O(n) circuit depth (Lemma 2), replacing exponential Trotter-Suzuki decomposition; (3) variable elimination reduces the constraint matrix dimension by removing variables with the most non-zero solution entries, shrinking qubit count and circuit depth at the cost of additional classical measurements. Evaluation is conducted on IBMQ Fez (159-qubit Heron r2), Sherbrooke, and Osaka (127-qubit Eagle r3) platforms, plus a classical GPU simulator (A100).
nv: Using the commute Hamiltonian as the QAOA driver Hamiltonian provides a universal hard-constraint encoding for arbitrary linear constraints, paired with a linear-complexity exact decomposition that makes it deployable on current NISQ hardware.

mx.speedup: 4.69x end-to-end over cyclic Hamiltonian-based QAOA on real IBMQ hardware
mx.accuracy: 235x improvement in success rate; 100% in-constraints rate; 658x improvement in approximation ratio gap vs. cyclic Hamiltonian
mx.other: 10^6x decomposition time reduction; circuit depth reduction from ~10^4 to ~100; 2.65x in-constraints rate improvement on IBMQ

th: commute Hamiltonian QAOA for constrained binary optimization

pb: Optimizing tensor programs for RISC-V vector extensions requires careful scheduling and loop transformations to exploit hardware parallelism. Hand-tuned optimizations are labor-intensive and may not generalize across different vector configurations.
me: Uses the MetaSchedule probabilistic framework to automatically search the scheduling space of tensor programs, applying loop tiling, vectorization, and memory optimization strategies optimized for RISC-V vector extensions.
nv: Application of MetaSchedule probabilistic scheduling to RISC-V vector extension, automating tensor program optimization.
th: Automated tensor program scheduling

t: Clay - open-source ASIP framework for microarchitecture-aware instruction customization with stateful behavior support
pb: Application-specific instruction processors (ASIPs) require manual microarchitecture design and instruction customization. Existing frameworks lack support for stateful behaviors and hardware-software co-optimization.
me: Clay provides an open-source framework for ASIP design that includes tools for instruction customization, microarchitecture specification, state management, and hardware-software simulation, enabling iterative optimization of instruction sets tailored to application requirements.
nv: Open-source ASIP framework with explicit support for stateful instruction behaviors and microarchitecture-aware customization.
th: Application-specific processor design framework

t: MM-GRADE - multi-modal RAG system for EDA tool documentation QA with vision LLM finetuning
pb: EDA tool documentation is complex and scattered across multiple formats (text, diagrams, screenshots). Users struggle to find accurate answers to technical questions about tool usage and configuration.
me: MM-GRADE integrates retrieval-augmented generation with vision LLM finetuning to process both textual documentation and visual materials (diagrams, screenshots), retrieving relevant multi-modal content and generating comprehensive answers through an LLM.
nv: Multi-modal RAG approach combining vision LLM finetuning for EDA tool documentation QA, enabling semantic search across mixed content types.
th: Multi-modal documentation Q&A system

t: QuickFlow: An Efficient Local Search Method to Map Convolutions on Spatial Architectures
pb: Mapping convolutions to spatial architectures requires exploring a vast mapping space with significant performance variations. Existing tools suffer from long execution times due to complex interactions between mapping decisions.
me: QuickFlow builds equivalences between mappings based on data reuse analysis and redesigns optimization around these equivalences. It performs greedy local search after quickly selecting best dataflow up to equivalence, and integrates an improved analytical model with exact tile-size formulas for arbitrary convolutions.
nv: Equivalence-based mapping optimization reducing search space through dataflow equivalence analysis.
th: Efficient dataflow-aware mapping for spatial accelerators

t: VeriRL: Boosting the LLM-based Verilog Code Generation via Reinforcement Learning
pb: LLM-based Verilog generation struggles with concurrency semantics, syntactic rigidity, and sparse/noisy simulation feedback, limiting hardware code quality.
me: Reinforcement learning framework with Trace-back based Rescore mechanism for reward reliability, sample-balanced weighting for catastrophic forgetting mitigation, and co-evolution of policy and reward models.
nv: First RL-driven approach for Verilog generation with iterative policy-reward co-evolution and trace-based feedback.
th: RL-optimized LLM-based Verilog code generation

t: Hyle: An HLS Framework for Hyperdimensional Computing Accelerators on FPGAs
pb: Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) offers efficient learning but lacks practical accelerator implementations, especially for cosine similarity and binary operations.
me: High-level synthesis framework targeting FPGA implementations. Specifically accelerates CGR (Cosine Similarity and Binary) operations. Automated synthesis from HDC algorithm specification to hardware.
nv: First HLS framework to efficiently accelerate HDC coprocessors on FPGAs, specifically targeting CGR and binary classifiers.
th: HLS framework for HDC FPGA accelerators

t: HLSDebugger: Identification and Correction of Logic Bugs in HLS Code with LLM Solutions
pb: Logic bugs in High-Level Synthesis code are difficult to identify and correct, slowing hardware design cycles.
me: LLM-based encoder-decoder architecture for bug identification, categorization, and correction. Trained on 300k HLS code samples with bugs. Distinguishes bug location, type, and generates fixes.
nv: First specialized LLM-based HLS debugger achieving 3x better bug correction than GPT-4.
th: LLM-based HLS code debugging

t: 3D CoSim: Coupled Operator Learning-Based Co-Simulator for Transferable 3D-IC Analysis
pb: Multi-physics analysis in 3D integrated circuits requires complex PDE simulations coupling electromagnetic and thermal fields, which are time-consuming and difficult to adapt to diverse design configurations. Existing neural network field solvers lack compatibility with complex, arbitrary 3D IC configurations.
me: Proposes 3D CoSim, a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) based simulator using a Multi-input DeepONet architecture to learn nonlinear mappings from geometrical and physical setups to multiphysics fields. The framework integrates heat equation, Maxwell's equations, and diverse boundary conditions to enable unified solutions for both electromagnetic and thermal fields. DeepONet learns transfer functions that generalize across different configurations.
nv: First PINN-based multi-physics simulator for arbitrary 3D IC configurations that achieves 844-7600× speedup over traditional COMSOL while maintaining 97% accuracy on EM and 99.8% on thermal simulations.
th: Neural multi-physics simulation for 3D ICs

t: ExactMap: Enhancing Delay Optimization in Parallel ASIC Technology Mapping
pb: Existing sequential ASIC technology mappers neglect load information during mapping, leading to significant discrepancy between estimated and actual cell delays and suboptimal performance. Sequential algorithms cannot exploit modern multicore and GPU parallelism.
me: Proposes ExactMap, a parallel ASIC technology mapper that: (1) considers load information of intermediate solutions to identify critical nodes, (2) selects delay-oriented cells based on load-aware delay estimation, (3) employs dual recovery method for both delay and area optimization, and (4) integrates optimization within configuration-level parallelism framework on GPU.
nv: First parallel ASIC technology mapper incorporating load-aware delay estimation and achieving 32% average delay reduction with 65.33× speedup on GPU.
th: Parallel delay-optimized technology mapping

t: HLSTester: Efficient Testing of Behavioral Discrepancies with LLMs for High-Level Synthesis
pb: High-level synthesis generates hardware from C/C++ programs with synthesis directives, but hardware-specific and platform-dependent characteristics can introduce behavioral discrepancies between original software and synthesized circuits. Existing testing methods require significant human effort and are immature.
me: Proposes HLSTester, an LLM-aided testing framework combining: (1) LLM-guided testbench generation from existing C/C++ tests, adapting syntax to HLS compatibility, (2) backward slicing to identify key variables in both C/C++ and HLS programs for runtime spectrum analysis, (3) dynamic mutation with LLM-based progressive reasoning for test input generation, and (4) redundancy-aware filtering to skip repetitive hardware testing.
nv: First LLM-aided testing framework for HLS behavioral verification that significantly accelerates testing while achieving higher pass rates than traditional methods.
th: LLM-aided HLS behavioral discrepancy testing

t: Revolution or Hype? Seeking the Limits of Large Models in Hardware Design
pb: Recent breakthroughs in Large Language Models and Large Circuit Models have created excitement about AI's potential in EDA, but significant skepticism remains about practical capabilities versus inflated expectations.
me: Panel paper synthesizing perspectives from leading experts in academia and industry to critically examine practical capabilities, fundamental limitations, and future prospects of large AI models in circuit design. Frames debate on reliability, scalability, and interpretability while evaluating whether these models meaningfully outperform or complement traditional EDA methods.
nv: Foundational overview paper providing authoritative perspective on capabilities and limitations of LLMs and large circuit models in EDA applications.
th: AI models in hardware design: capabilities and limitations

t: e-boost: Boosted E-Graph Extraction with Adaptive Heuristics and Exact Solving
pb: E-graph extraction for circuit synthesis requires expensive ILP solving. Existing methods are computationally limited and do not scale well.
me: Hybrid framework combining parallelized heuristics, adaptive pruning strategies, and ILP solving. Heuristics generate candidates; ILP refines optimal solutions. Achieves 558× speedup over pure ILP; 7.6-8.1% area improvement in synthesized circuits.
nv: Adaptive pruning combined with parallel heuristics and ILP for accelerated e-graph extraction with improved synthesis quality.
th: Hybrid e-graph extraction framework

t: LLM4Verilog: Building Large-Scale, High-Quality Data Infrastructure for Verilog Code Generation via Community Efforts
pb: High-quality training datasets for Verilog code generation are limited. Existing datasets lack scale and diversity for robust LLM fine-tuning.
me: Community-driven dataset collection and curation infrastructure for Verilog code generation. LLM fine-tuning on the dataset with pass@1 evaluation. Achieves 6.6-13.2% improvements in pass@1 metrics via fine-tuning.
nv: Large-scale community-driven Verilog dataset infrastructure for LLM training with demonstrated pass@1 improvements.
th: Verilog LLM dataset infrastructure

t: Diffusion-Model-Enhanced Layout Pattern Generation for Sub-3nm DFM
pb: Modern VLSI layout pattern generation for design for manufacturability (DFM) at sub-3nm nodes faces rapid evolution of intricate design rules and scarcity of high-quality, rule-compliant layout data during new process technology development.
me: Diffusion-based framework reframes complex layout synthesis as a sequence of template-guided inpainting tasks, significantly reducing training sample requirements. Leverages knowledge of a pre-trained image foundation model to generate layout variations satisfying complex 2D metal interconnect design rule constraints. Introduces novel template-based denoising scheme to eliminate residual noisy pixels. Uses few-shot fine-tuning to adapt to new technology nodes.
nv: Uses diffusion models as image foundation models for data-efficient layout pattern generation at sub-3nm nodes.
th: AI-enhanced layout design

t: Rhea: a Framework for Fast Design and Validation of RTL Cache-Coherent Memory Subsystems
pb: Designing and validating efficient cache-coherent memory subsystems is complex; there is a gap between high-level simulation fidelity and the reality of RTL hardware implementations.
me: Unified framework generating synthesizable, highly configurable RTL supporting various architectural parameters; integrates Verilator's cycle-accurate RTL simulation with gem5's full-system simulation enabling realistic workloads and operating systems to run alongside actual RTL under test. Hybrid co-simulation approach for improved fidelity over pure simulation.
nv: Gem5-Verilator co-simulation flow enabling realistic workload validation on RTL cache-coherent memory subsystems.
th: RTL memory subsystem design

t: HPVM-HDC: A Heterogeneous Programming System for Accelerating Hyperdimensional Computing
pb: Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) programs are manually written in target-specific languages (CUDA, C++, Python) that cannot be retargeted to HDC-specific accelerators (digital ASICs, ReRAM devices), and no programming system enables productive development with efficient code generation across CPUs, GPUs, and multiple HDC accelerators.
me: The system provides two components: HDC++, a C++-based DSL built on Hetero-C++ that exposes 24 HDC-specific primitives (hypervector/hypermatrix ops, Hamming distance, cosine similarity, encoding/training/inference loop constructs) in a target-agnostic unified programming model; and HPVM-HDC, a heterogeneous compiler that extends LLVM/HPVM IR with HDC-specific intrinsics and compiles HDC++ to CPUs (via HPVM CPU backend), GPUs (via CUDA/cuBLAS/Thrust), a 40nm digital HDC ASIC (Hamming-distance pipelined, 0.78 TOPS/W), and a ReRAM HDC accelerator simulator. Two approximation optimizations exploit HDC error resilience: automatic binarization propagation (taint analysis reducing element bitwidth to 1 bit) and reduction perforation (strided or segmented loop iteration over hypervector dimensions for Hamming/cosine similarity and matmul operations).
nv: HDC++'s high-level stage primitives (encoding_loop, training_loop, inference_loop) allow the same source to be lowered to coarse-grained accelerator instructions on ASICs/ReRAM and to fine-grained CUDA/HPVM IR on CPUs/GPUs, enabling the first execution of complete HDC applications on both a taped-out digital ASIC and a ReRAM accelerator.

mx.speedup: 1.17x geomean over optimized CUDA on GPU; up to 3.4x with approximation optimizations
mx.other: 1.6x reduction in total LOC across CPU+GPU baselines; first HDC application execution on digital ASIC and ReRAM accelerator

th: Retargetable HDC programming system with DSL and heterogeneous compiler

t: Caravan: A Hardware/Software Co-Design for Efficient SIMD Neighbor Search on Point Clouds
pb: Neighbor search in 3D point cloud processing via k-d trees is compute-intensive and exhibits SIMD underutilization: consecutive queries follow similar tree paths but diverge at deeper levels, causing sparse VPU lane usage that standard SIMD instructions cannot efficiently handle.
me: Caravan-SW batches consecutive neighbor search queries that visit similar k-d tree nodes and processes them in parallel using SIMD (AVX512) instructions. At deeper tree levels where query navigation diverges, Caravan-HW adds two new ISA instructions that enable re-indexing of valid (non-empty) SIMD lanes and fast operand shuffling, allowing dense SIMD operations on the remaining active lanes. The hardware modification is lightweight, requiring only 0.032 mm2 of additional silicon area.
nv: Two new ISA instructions that re-index and shuffle valid SIMD elements at divergent k-d tree leaf levels, eliminating the runtime sparsity penalty of batched neighbor search without a full custom accelerator.

mx.speedup: 5.19x neighbor search speedup (1.97x end-to-end) with Caravan-HW; 4.05x (1.85x end-to-end) with SW only
mx.area: 0.032 mm2 additional area for HW extension

th: SIMD-aware hardware/software co-design for k-d tree neighbor search

t: Concorde: Fast and Accurate CPU Performance Modeling with Compositional Analytical-ML Fusion
pb: Accurate CPU performance simulation (cycle-accurate or analytical) is extremely slow, while pure ML-based performance models are fast but lack accuracy and generalizability across microarchitectures and workloads. Neither approach alone satisfies the speed-accuracy requirements of design-space exploration for modern out-of-order processors.
me: Concorde fuses compositional analytical models with ML components in a hybrid framework: the analytical component captures first-principles microarchitecture behavior (pipeline stages, cache hierarchy, branch prediction, memory subsystem) using structured equations, while an ML model corrects residual prediction error from complex interactions not captured analytically. The fusion is compositional in that different analytical sub-models for each CPU pipeline stage are trained or parameterized independently and composed at inference time, allowing fast per-configuration evaluation. This is inferred from the title's 'Compositional Analytical-ML Fusion' framing; no abstract text was available for verification.
nv: Compositional fusion of per-stage analytical CPU models with ML correction terms, combining the interpretability and generalization of analytical models with the residual accuracy of learned components for fast CPU performance prediction.
th: Analytical-ML hybrid CPU performance modeling

t: Assassyn: A Unified Abstraction for Architectural Simulation and Implementation
pb: Architecture developers maintain two separate codebases—a simulation model for design-space exploration and an RTL implementation—creating coordination overhead, alignment errors, and duplicated effort that slow hardware development. Programming directly in RTL is error-prone and low-productivity, forcing teams to decouple modeling from implementation.
me: Assassyn provides a high-level, general-purpose programming framework built on asynchronous event handling—a behavioral model common to both hardware design and software engineering. Developers write a single Assassyn program; the framework compiles it to both a cycle-accurate simulator and synthesizable RTL, enforcing structural alignment by construction. The asynchronous event abstraction covers a broad class of architectures from pipeline components to out-of-order CPUs and application-specific accelerators.
nv: A single programming abstraction based on asynchronous event handling that simultaneously generates aligned cycle-accurate simulators and synthesizable RTL, eliminating the dual-codebase problem by construction.

mx.area: comparable perf/area to hand-crafted RTL; 6x perf/area vs. HLS-generated RTL
mx.other: 70% reduction in lines of code; 1.26x code overhead vs. hand-crafted RTL

th: unified simulation and RTL generation from a single abstraction

t: 24.1 A 12b 3GS/s Pipelined ADC with Gated-LMS-Based Piecewise-Linear Nonlinearity Calibration
pb: Pipelined ADCs using open-loop residue amplifiers suffer from large gain errors and severe gain nonlinearity; polynomial-based background calibration incurs significant power and area overhead, especially at high sampling rates (>1GS/s).
me: A piecewise-linear (PWL) nonlinearity calibration extracts coefficients in the background using gated LMS filters with adaptive thresholds, avoiding foreground calibration overhead and polynomial computation complexity. A dual-path amplification scheme improves settling accuracy and power efficiency.
nv: Background piecewise-linear nonlinearity calibration via gated LMS filters with adaptive thresholds, enabling high-speed calibration without polynomial computation or foreground overhead.
th: High-speed pipelined ADC with background LMS-based piecewise-linear calibration

t: A Crystal-Less Frequency-Modulation Transmitter IC with Joint Neural-Network-Driven Modulation and Coding for Low-Power Connectivity
pb: IoT transmitters suffer from high power consumption and complexity of PLL-based frequency modulation requiring crystal references, while crystal-less alternatives suffer carrier drift, phase noise, or need additional resonant devices.
me: Crystal-less FM transmitter using free-running LC oscillator with neural-network-driven modulation and coding jointly optimizing the transmit waveform to compensate for oscillator drift and phase noise while maintaining link reliability.
nv: Joint neural-network optimization of modulation and coding to compensate for uncontrolled oscillator behavior, eliminating crystal reference cost and power overhead.
th: neural-network-driven crystal-less FM transmitter for IoT

t: 19.9 An 11-to-16.4GHz, 3.4GHz/µs-Slope, 5.32GHz-Chirp-Bandwidth, 0.043%-RMS-Frequency-Error FMCW Digital PLL with Posterior-Segment DPD Featuring 5-Chirp-Cycle Convergence Time
pb: FMCW radars for autonomous driving and IoT require wide-bandwidth chirps with high linearity and fast convergence to multiple frequency bands; multi-vehicle interference and multi-mode operation demand rapid frequency-hopping and DPD convergence within single chirp bursts.
me: 11-to-16.4GHz digital PLL with posterior-segment digital predistortion (DPD) that converges in 5 chirp cycles, generating chirps with 3.4GHz/µs slope and 5.32GHz bandwidth, achieving 0.043% RMS frequency error despite nonlinearity.
nv: Posterior-segment DPD architecture that achieves 5-chirp-cycle convergence, enabling rapid frequency-hopping and multi-mode operation.
th: Fast-converging FMCW radar frequency-agile PLL

t: 25.3 AI-Enabled Design Space Discovery and End-to-End Synthesis for RFICs with Reinforcement Learning and Inverse Methods Demonstrating mm-Wave/sub-THz PAs Between 30 and 120GHz
pb: RF/mmWave IC design relies on intuitive, template-based architectures that limit exploration to small pre-fixed topologies. Circuit-EM co-design requires iterative trial-and-error optimization across transistor sizing, power-combining, matching-network design, and layout extraction. This severely restricts achievable performance and extends design time.
me: An AI-enabled algorithmic flow combines reinforcement learning for architecture discovery and inverse EM synthesis for passive network design. The system automates circuit topology selection, parameter optimization, and layout generation from specifications to fabricated silicon without manual template selection or iterative simulation loops.
nv: End-to-end AI-enabled RFIC synthesis with both active and passive optimization, from specifications to layout, demonstrating non-intuitive architectures.

mx.other: 34-70GHz: 21.2dBm Psat, 26% PAE; 100-120GHz: 12.6dBm Psat

th: AI-enabled RFIC design space discovery and synthesis

t: LLMulator: Generalizable Cost Modeling for Dataflow Accelerators with Input-Adaptive Control Flow
pb: Existing performance prediction methods for dataflow-based accelerators (TPUs, NPUs, FPGAs) fail to generalize across three dimensions: unseen applications with extreme loop scales (errors exceeding 40%), input-dependent control flows where branch probabilities shift at runtime (errors up to 60%), and diverse hardware architectures with varying memory delays and loop mapping primitives. No prior method unifies all three generalization axes.
me: LLMulator uses a pre-trained LLM (LLaMA-3.2-1B fine-tuned via LoRA) as the backbone for cost prediction with three novel mechanisms: (1) Progressive numeric encoding that tokenizes each decimal digit independently and uses categorical cross-entropy rather than regression to predict performance as digit-wise classification with beam-search error correction, enabling range-agnostic estimates; (2) Dynamic Prediction Calibration (DPC) using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)-style reinforcement learning with a replay buffer, where the model is updated online from Verilator simulation feedback to adapt to runtime input variations in loop bounds and control-flow branching; (3) A progressive dataset synthesizer that generates multi-level training data via AST-based generation, dataflow-specific loop-tree mutation, and LLM-based augmentation, then formats data with intermediate RTL reasoning chains (via SiliconCompiler and OpenROAD) to teach the model compilation-level reasoning.
nv: Treating hardware performance values as digit-wise categorical token sequences (rather than regression targets) enables confidence-aware, range-agnostic prediction that generalizes to out-of-distribution loop scales, combined with RL-based online calibration for input-adaptive control flows.

mx.accuracy: 12.2% MAPE on ASIC scenarios; 9.7% error reduction from DPC over static; 16.7%–7.8% error reduction vs GNNHLS/TLP

th: LLM-based generalizable cost modeling for dataflow accelerators

t: OmniSim: Simulating Hardware with C Speed and RTL Accuracy for High-Level Synthesis Designs
pb: High-Level Synthesis (HLS) tools cannot correctly simulate complex dataflow designs at the C level—particularly those with non-blocking FIFO accesses (read_nb/write_nb), infinite loops, and cyclic module dependencies—because the OS-level scheduling of software threads does not correspond to hardware timing, leading to incorrect functional results and inaccurate cycle counts; falling back to C/RTL co-simulation takes hours to days.
me: OmniSim introduces a multi-threaded simulation framework operating at the LLVM IR level. It classifies dataflow designs into three types (A: blocking-only/acyclic; B: non-blocking or cyclic but single-behavior; C: non-blocking with behavior depending on FIFO access outcome) and applies different simulation strategies accordingly. Key mechanisms: (1) one software thread per active dataflow module (Func Sim threads) plus a dedicated Performance Simulation thread (Perf Sim thread); (2) FIFO read/write timing tables that explicitly record the hardware cycle at which each FIFO event occurs, independent of OS thread scheduling; (3) a Query Pool where Func Sim threads pause on non-blocking FIFO accesses until the Perf Sim thread resolves the query by comparing hardware-cycle timestamps; (4) flexibly overlapped execution where Func Sim and Perf Sim threads run concurrently rather than in strict phases, yielding additional speedup. An LLVM pass instruments the IR to track basic block execution traces and rewrites dataflow functions to launch concurrent threads. Incremental simulation is supported to avoid full restarts when FIFO sizes change.
nv: A tightly coupled, flexibly overlapped multi-thread simulation framework where a dedicated performance simulation thread synchronizes non-blocking FIFO events using hardware-cycle timestamps stored in FIFO tables, enabling correct simulation of previously unsupported Type B and C HLS dataflow designs at near-C speed.

mx.speedup: up to 35.9x over C/RTL co-simulation; up to 6.61x over LightningSim
mx.accuracy: near-RTL accuracy (99.9% cycle accuracy maintained for Type A, functionally correct for Types B and C)
mx.other: Incremental FIFO-size DSE: 4 orders of magnitude speedup over full simulation; correctly simulates 11 designs previously unsupported by any HLS tool

th: C-speed RTL-accurate simulation for complex HLS dataflow designs

t: MUSS-TI: Multi-level Shuttle Scheduling for Large-Scale Entanglement Module Linked Trapped-Ion
pb: Compiling quantum circuits for Entanglement Module Linked Quantum Charge-Coupled Device (EML-QCCD) trapped-ion architectures is inefficient because existing compilers do not account for the distinct functional zones (storage, operation, optical/entanglement) within each QCCD module, leading to excessive ion shuttle operations and reduced circuit fidelity. Cross-module nonlocal gates via photonic fiber links further complicate qubit routing.
me: MUSS-TI constructs a dependency graph (DAG) of the quantum circuit and applies a multi-level scheduling strategy analogous to classical memory scheduling: storage zones map to L0 (disk), operation zones to L1 (memory), and optical zones to L2 (CPU). Gate selection prioritizes immediately executable gates; qubit routing assigns each qubit to the nearest-level available zone; conflict handling uses an LRU eviction policy to relocate the least-recently-used qubit to a lower-level zone. A look-ahead SWAP insertion algorithm (k=8 layers) strategically inserts SWAP gates between different QCCD modules to reduce long-range shuttle counts; a SABRE-inspired bidirectional initial mapping further reduces overhead.
nv: Applying the multi-level cache scheduling abstraction (LRU replacement, zone-level hierarchy) to trapped-ion qubit routing, where storage/operation/optical zones are treated as memory levels and qubit eviction mimics page replacement.

mx.speedup: 58.9% shorter execution time vs. baseline for small-scale circuits
mx.other: Shuttle operation reduction: 41.74% (30-32 qubits), 73.38% (117-128 qubits), 59.82% (256-299 qubits)

th: Zone-aware quantum circuit compilation for modular trapped-ion systems

t: ReGate: Enabling Power Gating in Neural Processing Units
pb: Modern NPU chips (e.g., Google TPU generations) waste 30-72% of their active energy on static (leakage) power because they lack fine-grained power management support; conventional CPU/GPU power-gating techniques do not transfer directly because NPUs use large systolic arrays with deterministic dataflows, software-managed SRAM scratchpads, in-order VLIW pipelines, and no dynamic instruction scheduling.
me: ReGate uses hardware-software co-design differentiated by component. For systolic arrays (SAs): non-zero weight detection generates row/column bitmaps (col_nz, row_nz), and a prefix-sum circuit derives which rows/columns should be powered off; PE-level power gating then follows the diagonal weight-stationary dataflow — the PE_on signal propagates diagonally from the SA input, overlapping wake-up with computation to expose only single-PE wake-up latency. For ICI and HBM controllers: a lightweight hardware-based idle-detection state machine gates these units between collective operators (AllReduce, AllGather). For vector units and SRAM: a new NPU ISA extension adds setpm instructions with three modes (on/auto/off) that let the ML compiler insert power-management instructions at statically-known idle boundaries — the compiler determines VU idle gaps from instruction scheduling and SRAM capacity from tile-size analysis.
nv: Diagonal-dataflow-aware cycle-level PE power gating in systolic arrays, where the PE_on signal propagates through the array following the inherent weight-stationary diagonal dataflow, enabling fine-grained power gating with only single-PE wake-up latency overhead.

mx.energy_or_tops_w: 8.5%-32.8% energy reduction (15.5% average) vs. no power gating
mx.other: <0.5% performance degradation; <3.3% area overhead; 31.1%-62.9% carbon emission reduction at fleet scale

th: Fine-grained NPU power gating via hardware-software co-design

t: StreamTensor: Make Tensors Stream in Dataflow Accelerators for LLMs
pb: Dataflow accelerators for LLMs (e.g., AMD Versal, SambaNova SN40L, IBM AIU) require manual effort to wire together kernels via on-chip FIFOs, manage external DMA access patterns, size FIFOs to prevent deadlock, and fuse kernels with compatible stream layouts — problems that compound across inter-kernel, multi-DMA, and large context-length LLM workloads, preventing end-to-end optimization.
me: StreamTensor is an MLIR-based compiler that introduces an iterative tensor (itensor) type encoding element shape, iteration space, and iteration map to uniquely capture a kernel's stream access order. The compilation pipeline proceeds through: (1) Linalg tiling and conversion to dataflow IR with itensor-typed kernel boundaries; (2) stream-based kernel fusion that compares producer/consumer itensor types — matching types are connected by FIFOs directly, mismatched types get minimal ping-pong buffer layout converters sized analytically from itensor types; (3) itensor folding to merge adjacent producer-consumer buffers; (4) iterative tensor vectorization to align FIFO bandwidth with kernel parallelism; (5) LP-based FIFO sizing that formulates token flow as a scheduling problem and solves it with linear programming to minimize FIFO depth while preventing deadlock; and (6) ILP graph partitioning for resource allocation. Three hierarchical design spaces (Linalg tiling, kernel fusion, resource allocation) are explored with Optuna blackbox optimization, intensity-aware unrolling, and heuristic permutation.
nv: The iterative tensor (itensor) type system that explicitly encodes streaming access order (iteration space + iteration map), enabling automated correctness-verified stream-based kernel fusion, minimal layout converter generation, and LP-based FIFO sizing for dataflow accelerators.

mx.speedup: Up to 0.76x lower latency than state-of-the-art FPGA LLM accelerators; 0.64x lower latency than GPUs
mx.energy_or_tops_w: Up to 1.99x higher energy efficiency compared to GPUs

th: Automated dataflow compiler for stream-based LLM acceleration on FPGAs

t: XaaS Containers: Performance-Portable Representation With Source and IR Containers
pb: Containers provide portability but sacrifice hardware-specific optimizations in HPC environments. Current containerization approaches force early-stage compilation decisions that limit performance across diverse HPC systems.
me: Proposes XaaS (Acceleration as a Service) containers using Source and Intermediate Representation (IR) representations. Delays performance-critical decisions until deployment time. t: Zero-Value Code Specialization via Profile-Guided Control Data Flow Analysis
pb: Zero-value propagation in programs causes redundant operations that severely impact performance. Since zero-values are generated dynamically at runtime, static analysis alone cannot eliminate these redundancies.
me: ZeroSpec: A profile-guided code optimizer that combines static control data flow analysis to identify zero-value propagation patterns with runtime profiling. Uses a fine-grained cost model to evaluate optimization potential and construct targeted fast paths.
nv: Efficient static control data flow analysis algorithm for identifying zero-value-induced redundancies; automated profile-guided specialization of fast paths; fine-grained cost model for optimization selection.
th: Software Optimization via Profiling

t: KVMSR+UDWeave: Extreme-Scaling with Fine-grained Parallelism on the UpDown Graph Supercomputer
pb: Irregular graph applications are challenging to program on scalable supercomputers. Achieving extreme-scale performance (million-fold parallelism) on skewed graphs requires new programming models and abstractions.
me: KVMSR+UDWeave: Novel programming model that cleanly separates parallelism, computation binding, and data placement. Leverages UpDown supercomputer features (computation location naming, shared global address space). Enables maximum parallelism expression.
nv: Separation of three parallel programming dimensions; exploitation of UpDown architecture features; expression of maximum parallelism for scalable graph algorithms; reduced programming effort for irregular workloads.
th: Irregular Graph Computing at Scale

t: The Cost of Teaching Operational ML
pb: Operational ML requires skills beyond model development, including infrastructure provisioning, distributed training, deployment, monitoring, and automation—capabilities grounded in HPC and distributed systems but lacking comprehensive educational frameworks.
me: Graduate-level course (ML Systems Engineering and Operations) using Chameleon Cloud testbed for hands-on infrastructure provisioning, distributed training, deployment, monitoring, and automation across 186,692 compute instance hours.
nv: First comprehensive cost analysis of operational ML education, documenting compute resource requirements and projecting commercial cloud costs for ML systems course.
th: ML Systems Education & Infrastructure

t: Mojo: MLIR-based Performance-Portable HPC Science Kernels on GPUs for the Python Ecosystem
pb: Scientific Python ecosystem lacks portable GPU programming with C-like performance. CUDA/HIP require language switching and target single vendors. Python abstractions (CuPy, Numba) sacrifice performance. Need for high-performance, portable, Python-integrated GPU programming.
me: Mojo language implementation leveraging MLIR compiler infrastructure with CUDA-like syntax for compile-time portable GPU programming. Evaluated on four scientific kernels: stencil (memory-bound), BabelStream (memory-bound), miniBUDE (compute-bound), Hartree-Fock (compute-bound with atomics).
nv: First comprehensive evaluation of Mojo for scientific GPU computing, demonstrating MLIR-based performance portability approach for Python ecosystem.
th: Performance-Portable GPU Programming

t: coMtainer: Compilation-assisted HPC Container Images with Enhanced Adaptability
pb: Containers simplify HPC deployment but fail to deliver optimal performance due to separated build/execution workflows, missing system-specific optimizations.
me: coMtainer embeds build-time information into containers, enabling remote HPC systems to specialize images with native toolchains and apply LTO/PGO optimizations.
nv: Compilation-assisted container transformation that preserves image neutrality while enabling system-specific optimization
th: Container & Deployment Optimization

t: Dynamic Thread Coarsening for CPU and GPU OpenMP Code
pb: Thread coarsening is well-known for GPU optimization but less explored for CPUs. Divergent control flow reduces effectiveness on both platforms. Existing approaches require compile-time uniformity proof, limiting applicability to real programs with data-dependent control flow.
me: Implement multi-level thread coarsening for CPU and GPU OpenMP code via generic LLVM IR transformation. Introduce dynamic convergence: generate both coarsened and non-coarsened code paths for divergent regions; runtime decision based on thread uniformity. Evaluate on HecBench (GPU) and LULESH (CPU).
nv: First dynamic thread coarsening approach handling divergent control flow; defers uniformity check to runtime.
th: Compiler-based thread-level optimization for heterogeneous code

t: PerfDojo: Automated ML Library Generation for Heterogeneous Architectures
pb: ML model performance tuning requires manual optimization across diverse hardware (CPUs: x86/Arm/RISC-V, GPUs, accelerators) with varying instruction sets, data types, and architecture-specific requirements. Manual approaches are resource-intensive; existing automated methods rely on complex heuristics and uninterpretable representations.
me: PerfLLM: automated optimization via LLMs and RL. Core innovation is PerfDojo—an RL environment using human-readable, mathematically-inspired code representation ensuring semantic validity through transformations. Framework optimizes kernels without prior hardware knowledge, enabling human analysis and RL training.
nv: First LLM+RL framework for portable performance optimization using semantically-valid, human-readable intermediate representation; avoids complex heuristics.

mx.focus: Performance gains across architectures, portability, optimization time

th: AI-driven automated performance optimization for heterogeneous systems

t: Enhancing ChatPORT with CUDA-to-SYCL Kernel Translation Capability
pb: Code translation for parallel programming models (CUDA to SYCL) remains largely unexplored despite LLMs' general code translation capabilities
me: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of 19 open-source code models (0.5-34B params) on CUDA-to-SYCL kernel pairs from heterogeneous computing benchmarks
nv: ChatPORT: fine-tuned LLMs for parallel kernel translation; demonstrates that modest fine-tuning significantly improves correctness from baseline ~0% to 19.9-81.7%
th: LLM-based code translation for heterogeneous computing

t: Determining Levels of Detail for Simulators of Parallel and Distributed Computing Systems via Automated Calibration
pb: Simulator accuracy depends on level of detail AND parameter calibration; trade-off between accuracy and complexity
me: Automated calibration framework; methodology for picking simulator detail levels; two case studies
nv: Automated calibration process; framework for level-of-detail selection across domains
th: Performance Modeling & Simulation

t: Constraint-Driven Auto-Tuning of GEMM-like Operators for MT-3000 Many-core Processor
pb: Optimizing deep learning operators, particularly GEMM-like operations, for emerging heterogeneous many-core processors like MT-3000 is challenging due to large search spaces and hardware-specific constraints. Existing approaches (hand-crafted libraries or general auto-tuners) are either expensive to develop or deliver sub-optimal performance.
me: DynaChain framework decouples computation and data movement for independent optimization with global data reuse maximization. Uses constraint dependency chains to dynamically eliminate invalid scheduling options during search. Applies integer linear programming (ILP)-based decomposition for irregular matrix dimensions. Hardware-aware micro-kernel design optimized for MT-3000's VLIW+SIMD architecture with improved register allocation and instruction pipelining.
nv: Constraint dependency chains dynamically prune search space; ILP-based decomposition handles irregular dimensions without padding; VLIW+SIMD-aware micro-kernel design with improved register allocation and pipelining.

mx.search_efficiency: Constraint chains significantly reduce search space
mx.development_complexity: Simplified kernel development vs. manual optimization

th: Automated Operator Optimization for Emerging Architectures

t: Preserving CUDA Syntax for SYCL Portability: A Thin C++ Abstraction without Kernel Migration
pb: Large-scale scientific applications must support multiple GPU architectures (NVIDIA, Intel), but converting CUDA code to SYCL requires significant effort and risks introducing bugs. Existing approaches either require full code translation or accept performance penalties.
me: Thin C++ abstraction layer preserving original CUDA kernel syntax and launch style while providing SYCL compatibility. Mechanical 'functorization' process converts CUDA to SYCL without full source translation. Evaluated on CRK-HACC (N-body cosmology code) across Polaris (NVIDIA) and Aurora (Intel) systems. Retains architecture-specific optimizations.
nv: Syntax-preserving abstraction enabling single-source CUDA/SYCL compilation without code duplication or automated translation; maintains original kernel structure and optimizations.

mx.performance: Competitive SYCL vs. native CUDA (specific values not in abstract)

th: GPU Portability & Multi-Architecture Abstraction

t: An MLIR pipeline for offloading Fortran to FPGAs via OpenMP
pb: HPC applications written in Fortran lack efficient pathways for offloading compute kernels to FPGAs for acceleration, requiring custom compilers and limiting portability.
me: MLIR-based compiler pipeline combining OpenMP dialect with High-Level Synthesis (HLS) dialect. Flang frontend parses Fortran; MLIR transforms code; HLS backend targets FPGA synthesis. Supports OpenMP target directives for selective offloading and manual kernel optimization.
nv: First implementation of selective Fortran code offloading to FPGAs via OpenMP target directive within MLIR ecosystem, leveraging MLIR composability for portable compilation.
th: Heterogeneous compilation for FPGA acceleration

t: Agentic AI vs ML-based Autotuning: A Comparative Study for Loop Reordering Optimization
pb: Traditional ML-based autotuning approaches for HPC code optimization require expensive compile-run evaluations and lack adaptability for large applications. Emerging Agentic AI systems offer alternative optimization paradigms with unclear practical advantages.
me: Comparative analysis between traditional ML autotuner and novel LoopGen-AI agent system using three LLMs (GPT-4.1, Claude 4.0, Gemini 2.5). Evaluation on loop-level optimization (loop reordering). Prompt engineering with Persona + Context Manager patterns. Analysis of convergence, sample efficiency, and decision quality.
nv: First systematic comparison of Agentic AI (LLM-based agents) vs. traditional ML autotuning for HPC optimization, demonstrating Agentic AI's competitive performance with minimal program runs.

mx.agentic_ai_convergence: few program runs to competitive performance
mx.ml_autotuning_requirement: orders of magnitude more runs for peak performance
mx.prompt_engineering_impact: significant effectiveness increase with Persona + Context Manager patterns

th: Agentic AI for HPC code optimization

t: ATLAHS: An Application-centric Network Simulator Toolchain for AI, HPC, and Distributed Storage
pb: Existing network simulators rely on synthetic microbenchmarks or are domain-specific, limiting their ability to provide comprehensive performance insights for realistic AI, HPC, and storage workloads.
me: Introduce ATLAHS, a flexible, open-source simulation toolchain that traces real applications and simulates their workloads using the Group Operation Assembly Language (GOAL) format. Support multiple simulation backends and multi-job/multi-tenant scenarios.
nv: GOAL-based trace format for portable workload representation; application-centric simulation supporting AI, HPC, and storage; demonstrated accuracy with <5% error; outperforms AstraSim in runtime and efficiency.

mx.comparison: outperforms AstraSim in runtime and trace size

th: Network Simulation & Performance Modeling

t: MPPI - Type safe C++ Datatypes for MPI
pb: MPI's C-API requires users to manually describe buffer memory layouts for communication, which is error-prone and lacks type safety in modern object-oriented C++ code.
me: MPPI: C++-API and datatype engine leveraging C++20 concepts, ranges, and upcoming reflection to extract datatype information at compile-time; automatic MPI datatype construction.
nv: Compile-time MPI datatype extraction from C++ types using modern language features (concepts/reflection), eliminating manual datatype specification.
th: Type-safe C++ MPI API via compile-time datatype extraction

t: Connected-Component Labeling Using HLS for High-Energy Particle Physics Instruments
pb: High-level synthesis (HLS) can reduce FPGA development time, but effectiveness for complex signal processing kernels (like island detection) is unclear.
me: HLS implementation of island detection with 1D/2D configurations and 4-way/8-way connected-component labeling; report resource usage, throughput, and required optimizations.
nv: Empirical evaluation of HLS effectiveness for particle physics signal processing, identifying optimizations needed for high-throughput implementations.
th: HLS for particle physics signal processing kernels on FPGAs

t: A Compute Graph Simulation and Implementation Framework Targeting AMD Versal AI Engines
pb: Developing AI Engine (AIE) applications for AMD Versal requires separate host/accelerator codebases using AMD Vitis; this complicates development and integration with existing C++ code.
me: Framework with two components: (1) compute graph simulation library in C++, (2) Clang-based source-to-source translator. Enables embedding AIE prototypes in C++, auto-transforms to AIE projects.
nv: Unified C++ framework for AIE development; source-to-source translation eliminates manual host/accelerator separation; leverages C++ compile-time code execution.
hw: AMD Versal SoCs with AI Engines
th: Unified C++ framework for AMD Versal AI Engine development

t: CaRDS: Compiler-aided Remote Data Structures
pb: Conservative compile-time policies for far memory placement harm performance when memory is constrained
me: Compiler-runtime hybrid: static analysis identifies candidate objects, runtime determines remoting/prefetch/evacuation policies at data structure granularity
nv: Dynamic far memory policies at data structure granularity combining compile-time static analysis with runtime adaptation
th: Memory Hierarchy & Compiler Optimization

t: Testing and Benchmarking Emerging Supercomputers via the MFC Flow Solver
pb: New supercomputers require systematic testing and evaluation; lack of portable, user-friendly benchmarking tools limits adoption validation.
me: Multicomponent Flow Code (MFC) with automated toolchain for compilation, regression testing, and benchmarking across diverse hardware.
nv: Portable CFD benchmarking framework that automatically identifies compiler bugs and performance regressions on emerging supercomputers.
